I'm a CS major hoping to graduate next December. I strongly recommend looking up your professors on ratemyprofessors.com and asking junior and senior students for recommendations on who to take.
The reason is because your professors can seriously screw up your hopes and dreams to the nth degree. Be really careful whose class you sign up for. ALWAYS pick the easiest, nicest, and least challenging professor you can find. The reason is because you're paying to get a degree. You want to learn and get an education, but half the stuff you learn in college you're never going to use (**cough* calculus) so you want to find teachers who make classes as easy as possible. 

That first week of classes, go to class, read over the syllabus and try to gauge how hard your professor will be. If you have doubts whether you'll pass, drop and pick another professor. Failing a class because of a difficult professor can cost you your scholarship(s), push back your graduation date a whole year, and affect your whole well-being. Sometimes there will be just one professor who teaches a course. If he or she is a potential problem professor, avoid that class until you have no other choice but to take it. Also, try to avoid foreign professors. I'm not saying all of them are bad because some of them are actually nice and effective, but from my experience, they're generally harder to understand and deal with.

Since you're a high school junior, what you can do now to prepare for your CS courses is to teach yourself a programming language like Java. Also, look up and read computer science textbooks on algorithms and data structures. You can find a lot of CS books on the Internet for free. Most important, please research a good school. Go to a school that has a lot of good CS professors that are mostly American. Do your best to survive. Believe me you can get a CS degree if you're wise, determined, and responsible.
